title: [Mouse Without Borders] Hide mouse option fails to fully hide cursor on screen leave

judgment.rationale: The public sequence is clear and the implementation deliberately moves the cursor near the reported location, but the artifact's rendering source is not established.
evidence: With Hide mouse at screen edge enabled, moving to a second device makes the local cursor visibly jump to top center and leaves an artifact.
The report includes screenshots and a concrete two-device sequence.

HideMouseCursor sets the local cursor position near the top center and updates a fake cursor in https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/Common.cs.

fix_assessment.rationale: The public sequence is clear and the implementation deliberately moves the cursor near the reported location, but the artifact's rendering source is not established.

proposed_fixes.title: Remove the cursor artifact when leaving a machine
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The deliberate cursor repositioning or fake-cursor update may contribute to the visible artifact; the actual rendering path is not yet confirmed.
plan: Reproduce the screen transition and capture the order of native cursor movement and fake-cursor rendering.
Identify whether the artifact is a stale fake cursor, native cursor rendering, or display-driver behavior.
Adjust only the confirmed hide/cleanup path and add regression coverage for repeated machine switches and return.
verification: Leaving the local screen hides the cursor without a lingering artifact, and returning restores correct cursor position and visibility.
